structure_and_depth.location: analysis/outline.md: Research question and selection; Report structure 1–8; AIDD-U1–U4; Necessary source work and concrete limits.
structure_and_depth.basis:
Read the full original case, effective requirements, frozen outline, common assignment instructions and outline production history. The research question joins identifiable computational contributions to experimental/clinical testing and to the organization of the next decisive experiment. Candidate–indication–formulation, dated milestones and aliases provide a stable comparison unit; the purposive seven-case selection includes discontinued and inconclusive paths and is expressly not used to infer an industry success rate.
Sections 2–5 connect target prioritization, molecular proposal, synthesis, functional testing, optimization and experimental feedback to three distinct histories: new molecules, repositioning and boundary cases. Keeping baricitinib treatment evidence separate from AI's causal contribution and halicin as a research lead separate from a clinical candidate prevents inappropriate cross-stage conclusions. The clinical dossiers plan to retain endpoint hierarchy, analysis population, comparator, follow-up and termination rationale rather than reduce progress to phase labels.
Section 6 creates the actual synthesis across those dossiers: comparable stages, historical controls, prior exposure, selection, censoring and clock definitions. Original denominators are required before discussing aggregate success estimates. Section 7 and U2/U4 connect rights, laboratory responsibility, decisions, feedback access and termination to scientific execution; upfronts, contingent amounts, royalties, received cash and accounting revenue are kept distinct. Section 8 converts these into bounded engagement, co-discovery, licensing or deferral decisions tied to a falsifiable milestone.
The planned alias/status register, dated chains, clinical-design table and rights/payment matrix have complementary uses. The source-work section identifies missing originals and registry histories and limits unverified inferences without abandoning positive evidence. No necessary structural correction was found at outline scope. This is not verification of any clinical claim, cutoff status, partnership term or completed manuscript; those are explicitly still subject to the planned original-source work.

domain.basis: This is a local AIDD-U1 assessment in drug discovery, trial design and missing-data interpretation, not whole-report approval. Checked Nature Medicine patient disposition, safety results, original Table 2 and its footnotes, secondary outcomes, discussion, eligibility and statistical methods; n=71, allocation 18/18/18/17, completion 16/12/12/15, AE discontinuation 1/5/4/2 and week-12 missing 5/6/8/3 are supported and distinct. Liver withdrawals, concomitant nintedanib, three versus one exacerbations, and limits of biomarkers are interpreted cautiously. Viewed all four actual rendered Reporting Summary pages: page 2 gives the safety-based sample-size rationale and separate two-baseline-outlier sensitivity analysis; pages 3–4 specify the trial and endpoints. Page 4 only completes the exploratory proteomic timepoints and contains an unfilled plant template, so it supplies no missing clinical qualification. However the main text conflates observed-case FVC changes with the distinct ANCOVA/multiple-imputation results; original Figure 2 and the registered result denominators establish the necessary correction below. Read raw NCT05938920 protocol modules and its absolute-FVC result, and NCT07687459 identification/status/design/arms/outcomes: oral phase III recruiting, actual start 2026-09-09, estimated n=320 and 52-week annual decline endpoint are supported. The official 2026-09-10 announcement confirms first dosing; April inhalation clearance is a separate proposed phase I branch. No phase III efficacy or inhaled enrollment is inferred. Full protocol/SAP remain unavailable and were not represented as read.

findings.location: analysis/U1-rentosertib.md lines 35–37, from 'a reported mean FVC change of +98.4 mL' through 'the highest-dose signal combines observed measurements with an assumption about missing outcomes'.
findings.basis: R_TASK requires preservation of clinical result denominators and study-design limitations. The +98.4 mL and −20.3 mL values, and hence the 118.7 mL subtraction, are observed-case changes in Nature Medicine Figure 2a: the 60 mg QD group has n=10 and placebo n=14, not the full randomized n=18/17. Figure 2b separately gives baseline-adjusted ANCOVA with multiple imputation under MAR for all randomized patients: +89.2 mL (95% CI −8.7 to 187.2) and −8.2 mL (−98.1 to 81.7). NCT05938920 raw resultsSection/outcomeMeasuresModule, 'Absolute Change From Baseline in FVC in L', independently preserves observed denominators 10/14 and means 0.0984/−0.0203 L, followed by LS means 0.0892/−0.0082 L. The draft correctly warns that a within-group interval is not a between-group test, but its adjacent wording presents the quoted observed-case signal as though it already incorporates imputation and omits the adjusted result. This obscures the effect of missingness on the estimate and uncertainty. Label the first values and 118.7 mL as an observed-case comparison with their denominators; separately state the adjusted/imputed means and their actual uncertainty, maintaining the distinction from a between-group confidence interval. If subtracting the adjusted means, 97.4 mL is also only a descriptive difference unless a proper contrast estimate is supplied. Retain the existing MAR/MNAR and longer-trial cautions. This correction requires accurate reporting of the existing evidence, not a new clinical analysis.
